data.narrative:
Compound Eye is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jason Devitt and Haoyang Wang that has raised $20.6M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including same-stage companies Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $39M. Peer-median valuation across three same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the direct comparability of the three selected companies.

The two methods produce a wide valuation range: $33M (low), $895M (median), and $2.0B (high). The stage-progression result sits materially below peer benchmarks, reflecting the early capital deployed relative to peer valuations at this stage. The peer-median of $1.8B represents the most defensible central estimate, though the $1.6B–$2.0B peer range underscores significant uncertainty. Key variables include Compound Eye's revenue traction, customer concentration, and technology differentiation relative to named peers, none of which are quantified in available data.
